tools.name: adopt
tools.description: Adopt this profile's gateway: native login → mint an Administrator-level API key (idempotent by name) → wire the gateway's read/write permissions → live-probe the key → persist the credential (OS keyring, env-var fallback). Re-run on an adopted gateway is an all-skip no-op. Composition flags ride the bootstrap: --project deploys the CLI's WebDev routes, --checkout lands every enabled project locally, --bake saves a restore-ready gwbk

tools.name: api_call
tools.description: Call any gateway REST endpoint raw: `--method`/`--path` are the request, `--data`/`--header`/`--query` shape it, and the envelope's `data.result.data` is the gateway's JSON VERBATIM (no field dropped, no value coerced, key order preserved — the README's documented contract exception). Auth-pattern headers (`Authorization`, `X-Ignition-API-Token`, `Cookie`) are refused pre-I/O — credentials come from the profile

tools.name: backup_download
tools.description: Download a gwbk backup (streamed to disk)

tools.name: backup_restore
tools.description: Restore a gwbk onto THIS gateway — destructive, refused without --yes; the gateway restarts and blocks for minutes after the restore

tools.name: connections
tools.description: List database/OPC connections with healthcheck status as reported

tools.name: diagnostics_bundle_download
tools.description: Download the bundle ZIP (streamed to disk; the request rides a 300 s per-request timeout — the 30 s client default would truncate MB-sized bundles)

tools.name: diagnostics_bundle_generate
tools.description: Start bundle generation (POST, no body) — the 200 answer IS the fresh status (live capture: `{"state":"Generating"}`); generation takes ~2–6 s on a fresh rig, so pair with `wait`

tools.name: diagnostics_bundle_status
tools.description: The bundle status: `state` rides the CAPTURED vocabulary (`Generating` / `Valid` — unknown future states pass through verbatim, never refused); `fileSize` (bytes) appears only when `Valid`

tools.name: diagnostics_bundle_wait
tools.description: Poll the status until a terminal captured state (`Valid`) — an UNKNOWN state (outside the captured vocabulary) keeps polling honestly until the deadline; deadline expiry is exit 4 `network_error` (the restart-wait convention, no new slug) with the last observed state in the message

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Diagnose the gateway setup: URL, liveness, commissioning, auth, permissions, write, WebDev route, rig — exits 0 whenever the diagnosis completes (failing checks are data)

tools.name: e2e_doctor
tools.description: Diagnose the browser-E2E setup: node (≥20), npm, @playwright/test in the scaffold, a downloaded chromium, the gateway's testing bundle, and the gateway's trial state. Read-only and offline-safe — **exits 0 whenever the diagnosis completes**, so every finding is a `checks[]` row rather than an exit code. The two gateway rows report `skip` when no profile resolves or no --project is given

tools.name: e2e_init
tools.description: Scaffold a Playwright E2E suite into DIR (default ./e2e): a runner config, a global setup that logs in through `ign session login` and gates on `ign testing run`, gateway tag/ script helpers, an example suite, a .gitignore, and a README — then `npm install`. **Idempotent**: an existing file is reported `skipped` and never overwritten. Requires the global --yes; without it the verb writes nothing, spawns nothing, and refuses exit 2 after previewing every file and both commands

tools.name: eam_history
tools.description: EAM task run history (the gateway's own newest-first order)

tools.name: eam_task_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a task's PENDING execution (TASK-scoped). Refused exit 2 without --yes with the blast-radius preview in the message; nothing pending is an honest no-op (`fired: false`), a `canCancel: false` row reports the gateway's own refusal

tools.name: eam_task_delete
tools.description: Delete a task definition — signature-keyed (the gateway refuses a stale signature), behind the same --yes guard. Refused exit 2 without --yes with the blast-radius preview in the message

tools.name: eam_task_force
tools.description: Force-dispatch a task NOW — destructive, refused without --yes (it dispatches to the agent targets immediately). The confirmation prompt (and every refusal) carries the blast-radius preview line

tools.name: eam_task_modify
tools.description: Rewrite targeted keys of a task definition — the full-record read-modify-write (every key the gateway answered rides back; only the targeted keys change). Rename is deliberately ABSENT (the wire answers PUT-rename with 404 — see README's create-new + delete-old composite). Refused exit 2 without --yes with the blast-radius preview in the message

tools.name: eam_task_new
tools.description: Create a task definition (scheduleMode defaults to OnDemand — never auto-fires)

tools.name: eam_task_resume
tools.description: Resume a suspended task definition — the suspend inverse (TASK-scoped, like suspend). Refused exit 2 without --yes with the blast-radius preview in the message

tools.name: eam_task_suspend
tools.description: Suspend a task definition's scheduled dispatches — TASK-scoped runtime verb (there is NO agent-level suspend on the wire; an "agent" is suspended by suspending its tasks). Refused exit 2 without --yes, the blast-radius preview in the refusal message; on a stock gateway the runtime seam honestly refuses `eam_not_controller` (exit 6)

tools.name: eam_tasks
tools.description: Task definitions: bare `ign eam tasks` lists; with a name shows one definition + its scheduled state

tools.name: gan_status
tools.description: The GAN overview: total/running connections, in/out byte rates, remote gateways — all zeros are healthy data on a non-GAN gateway (the capture IS the canonical shape)

tools.name: license_status
tools.description: License inventory + trial state in ONE command: the hardware-key item rows and effective stamp ride the `/licenses` read, the license mode + countdown ride the trial companion (the mode is NOT on the licenses payload — capture fact)

tools.name: lint
tools.description: Lint local project files by delegating to ignition-lint (PATH discovery) — doctor posture: findings are DATA, exit 0 whenever the tool ran; --strict passes the tool's exit code through for CI

tools.name: logs
tools.description: Query, tail, and download gateway logs; manage logger levels

tools.name: logs_download
tools.description: Download the log archive — a SQLite .idb, never a zip

tools.name: logs_loggers
tools.description: List loggers / manage logger levels

tools.name: logs_loggers_reset
tools.description: Reset ALL logger levels to defaults — refused without --yes

tools.name: logs_loggers_set
tools.description: Set one logger's level — a mutation, refused without --yes

tools.name: metrics
tools.description: Gateway performance metrics (current gauges + thread counts)

tools.name: modules
tools.description: List gateway modules (healthy by default)

tools.name: profile_add
tools.description: Add (or overwrite) a gateway profile

tools.name: profile_list
tools.description: List configured profiles

tools.name: profile_use
tools.description: Switch the active profile

tools.name: project_copy
tools.description: Copy a project with all its resources

tools.name: project_delete
tools.description: Delete a project — destructive, refused without --yes

tools.name: project_diff
tools.description: Compare a project across two gateway profiles — statuses are B-relative-to-A (`added` = in B only, `removed` = in A only, `changed` = differing after resource.json normalization)

tools.name: project_export
tools.description: Export a project as a ZIP archive (streams to disk)

tools.name: project_import
tools.description: Import a project from a ZIP archive

tools.name: project_list
tools.description: List every runnable project: name, title, enabled, parent, inheritable (inheritance info from the items themselves)

tools.name: project_new
tools.description: Create a project (only provided fields ride the create body)

tools.name: project_rename
tools.description: Rename a project (native rename, not copy+delete)

tools.name: project_set
tools.description: Set project fields — --parent IS the inheritance move (reparent)

tools.name: project_sync
tools.description: Promote selected resources from profile A into profile B (direction is ALWAYS A→B) — destructive on B: the whole project is overwrite-imported, refused without --yes

tools.name: redundancy_status
tools.description: The flat redundancy status: role, project state, peer connection, config access, sync/failover pending, uptime (ms since gateway start — capture-proven) and last-sync (the `-1` never-synced sentinel on fresh rigs)

tools.name: resource_delete
tools.description: Delete one resource — destructive, refused without --yes

tools.name: resource_get
tools.description: Read one resource: JSON pretty-printed, text raw — binary (data.bin-class) resources refuse with exit 6

tools.name: resource_list
tools.description: List a project's resources (one path per line in human mode)

tools.name: resource_put
tools.description: Write one resource (upsert: created if absent, replaced if present) — JSON if parseable (application/json), else UTF-8 text (text/plain); binary-looking input refuses

tools.name: restart
tools.description: Restart the gateway — destructive, refused without --yes; --wait polls until RUNNING

tools.name: rig_down
tools.description: Stop the rig (compose down --remove-orphans; volumes KEPT — `reset` owns the teardown half)

tools.name: rig_logs
tools.description: Stream the rig's container logs (compose logs passthrough — raw lines, no envelope in any mode; the third streaming exception, README-documented)

tools.name: rig_reset
tools.description: Tear the rig down AND remove its volumes (down -v --remove-orphans), then bring it back up fresh — destructive, refused without --yes; no stale project/trial state survives

tools.name: rig_restore
tools.description: Restore a gwbk onto the rig's gateway — destructive, refused without --yes; synchronous restore + restart, then a witnessed RUNNING wait

tools.name: rig_snapshot
tools.description: Snapshot the rig's gateway: native gwbk (roaming backup, streamed) + per-project exports + manifest.json, composed in a timestamped directory — repeatable state

tools.name: rig_status
tools.description: Structured status: services, ports, volumes (allowlist JSON; a down rig is exit-0 data)

tools.name: rig_trial_reset
tools.description: Reset an EXPIRED trial to a fresh window — destructive, refused without --yes. Mechanism ladder: API-token POST (IGNITION_TOKEN) → native gateway login (--user / IGNITION_USER + IGNITION_PASSWORD). Non-expired trials refuse (trial_not_expired)

tools.name: rig_trial_status
tools.description: Show the trial state: licenseMode, trialState, seconds left, expired — plus the banners cross-check. No credential needed (the endpoints answer unauthenticated — fresh-rig friendly)

tools.name: rig_up
tools.description: Bring the rig up (compose up -d --wait) and wait for the gateway: RUNNING, or uncommissioned-as-data (exit 0 + wizard hint in warnings)

tools.name: script_run
tools.description: Execute gateway-side Python (Jython) — non-interactive, the route's entire purpose

tools.name: session_login
tools.description: Log in to the gateway and return the live session: the `webui-sid-*` cookie name and value, the CSRF token for `X-CSRF-Token`, the gateway URL, and `storage_state` — a Playwright `storageState` document ready to write straight to disk and point `use.storageState` at. The password is env-only (`IGNITION_PASSWORD`; missing exits 3, rejected exits 5). The cookie value and CSRF token are exposed ONLY under the global --json flag

tools.name: sessions
tools.description: List gateway sessions (designers, Perspective, Vision) — or terminate one via the `terminate` subcommand

tools.name: sessions_terminate
tools.description: Terminate (designer: prune / vision: close) a session — destructive, refused without --yes

tools.name: status
tools.description: Gateway status: identity, platform, uptime, license (incl. trial countdown)

tools.name: tags_alarms_ack
tools.description: Acknowledge alarms (explicit --username: the 3-arg wire form needs it). NOT --yes-guarded — acknowledging never un-acknowledges anything

tools.name: tags_alarms_active
tools.description: List active alarms — eventId/source/state/priority/name

tools.name: tags_alarms_history
tools.description: Query alarm history — requires a journal-provisioned gateway (default rigs refuse with the provisioning hint naming the missing chain)

tools.name: tags_browse
tools.description: Browse tags as a tree (Property children filtered by default) — providers appear at the root; needs the deployed routes (`ign webdev deploy`) — or run fully OFFLINE against an export via --from-export

tools.name: tags_config_create
tools.description: Create a tag from a JSON definition file (`-` = stdin) — aborts on an existing node (collision policy 'a')

tools.name: tags_config_delete
tools.description: Delete tag configurations — destructive, refused without --yes (the guard fires before ANY resolution: zero network work)

tools.name: tags_config_get
tools.description: Get a tag's configuration as (pretty) JSON — stringified value/defaultValue sub-dicts re-parsed into real JSON

tools.name: tags_export
tools.description: Export tag subtrees — json writes the gateway's native JSON interchange (the lossless round-trip); xml passes the gateway's own XML through byte-for-byte; csv is CLI-GENERATED and LOSSY (no alarms, legacy 48-column set, numeric enums — the gateway cannot export CSV)

tools.name: tags_history_query
tools.description: Query historical tag values — t_stamp + one column per tag; structurally safe anywhere (data requires a provisioned historian)

tools.name: tags_import
tools.description: Import a tag export into a target provider — json is the native interchange; xml/csv ride the gateway's importTags passthrough. A loss scan reports what xml/csv would drop or coerce BEFORE the import and refuses exit 2 unless --yes. Collision behavior: abort (default) refuses on collisions; overwrite replaces them (destructive: requires --yes)

tools.name: tags_provider_create
tools.description: Create a STANDARD tag provider (DB-backed providers are out of scope at MVP)

tools.name: tags_provider_delete
tools.description: Delete a tag provider — destructive, refused without --yes

tools.name: tags_provider_list
tools.description: List the gateway's tag providers (tag counts + health)

tools.name: tags_read
tools.description: Read one or more tag values (quality and timestamp included) — needs the deployed routes

tools.name: tags_udt_def
tools.description: Get a UDT definition (parameters + nested children, recursive)

tools.name: tags_udt_types
tools.description: List the provider's UDT types

tools.name: tags_write
tools.description: Write a value to a tag — the value is parsed as a JSON scalar (number/bool/null); anything unparseable is sent as a string; arrays/objects refuse — needs the deployed routes

tools.name: testing_run
tools.description: Run the gateway-side Jython test suite and return the machine verdict (exit 0 green, exit 6 red with the FULL results still in the envelope)

tools.name: version
tools.description: Print version information (CLI always; gateway check when a profile resolves)

tools.name: wait_gateway
tools.description: Wait until the gateway reports RUNNING (unauthenticated StatusPing — works even when auth is broken or absent)

tools.name: wait_module
tools.description: Wait until a module reports ACTIVE

tools.name: wait_restart
tools.description: Wait for a restart to complete — restart-aware: shares `restart --wait`'s semantics (non-RUNNING observed once → RUNNING; a 5 s floor guards the all-RUNNING case)

tools.name: webdev_deploy
tools.description: Deploy the embedded route bundle into the dedicated project (overwrite-replace — the CLI owns that project wholesale)

tools.name: webdev_status
tools.description: Probe every route's version handshake — a READ: exit 0 whenever the sweep completes, per-route degradation is data

tools.name: workspace_checkout
tools.description: Check out a project's resources to a local tree — mapped paths + the recorded `.ign-workspace.json` manifest + an idempotent `.gitignore` (manifest committed; codec artifacts ignored). Read-only on the wire: one export GET, zero imports

tools.name: workspace_push
tools.description: Push local edits to the gateway — guarded (refused without --yes; the refusal message IS the blast-radius preview); conflicts refuse EVEN WITH --yes (manual reconciliation); deletions need --delete (default: reported, skipped); untracked files are never imported; an empty selection writes nothing

tools.name: workspace_status
tools.description: Report workspace drift against the gateway — states are PUSH-RELATIVE (each row names what push would do: write / leave / refuse); the project comes from the workspace manifest, never re-typed. Read-only: one export GET
